records.gloss: For the director, of [the] sons of Korah, a psalm.
pieces: For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

L.1: For the director: of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

R.1: For the leader of the music. A song from the family of Korah.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: the sons of Korah: a family of Levite singers
decisions.reason: The descendants of Korah, a Levite (Numbers 26:11), served as gatekeepers and singers at the temple (1 Chronicles 9:19; 2 Chronicles 20:19). Eleven psalms carry their name (42-49, 84-85, 87-88). "Of" may mean the psalm belongs to their collection or was written by one of them.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1, Readable says what a psalm is.

records.heading: God goes up as King of all the earth

records.source: כָּֽל־הָ֭עַמִּים תִּקְעוּ־כָ֑ף הָרִ֥יעוּ לֵ֝אלֹהִ֗ים בְּק֣וֹל רִנָּֽה׃
records.gloss: All the peoples, strike [the] palm; shout to God with [the] sound of a ringing cry.
pieces: All you peoples, clap your hands! Raise a shout to God with ringing cries of joy!

L.2: All [you] peoples, clap [your] hands; shout to God with the sound of a ringing cry.

R.2: People of every nation, clap your hands! Cheer for God with loud, happy voices!

decisions.choice: clap and shout: the welcome given to a king
decisions.reason: Clapping and shouting greeted a new king (2 Kings 11:12; 1 Samuel 10:24). The psalm calls the nations to acclaim God as King (verses 3, 8-9).

decisions.choice: all the peoples: every nation, not Israel only
decisions.reason: The call goes out to the whole world, which the psalm sees gathering to God at the end (verse 10).

decisions.choice: a ringing cry: a loud shout of joy
decisions.reason: The word (rinnah) is a loud, ringing cry, here of joy.

records.source: כִּֽי־יְהוָ֣ה עֶלְי֣וֹן נוֹרָ֑א מֶ֥לֶךְ גָּ֝דוֹל עַל־כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: For YHWH, Most High, [is] to be feared, a great king over all the earth.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} Most High inspires awe; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the great King who rules the whole earth.

L.3: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [the] Most High, [is] to be feared, a great King over all the earth.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God who is above all, is wonderful and fearsome. He is the great King who rules the whole world.

decisions.choice: to be feared: awe-inspiring
decisions.reason: The word (nora') describes what fills people with awe and fear, here God's power as King.

decisions.choice: a great king: the title of an emperor
decisions.reason: "The great king" was the title of emperors who ruled many lesser kings, such as the king of Assyria (Isaiah 36:4). The psalm gives the title to the LORD over the whole earth.

decisions.choice: Most High: God above all
decisions.reason: As in 46:5.

decisions.choice: the God who is above all
decisions.reason: As in 46:5.

records.source: יַדְבֵּ֣ר עַמִּ֣ים תַּחְתֵּ֑ינוּ וּ֝לְאֻמִּ֗ים תַּ֣חַת רַגְלֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: He subdues peoples under us, and nations under our feet.
pieces: He brings peoples under our rule and lays nations at our feet.

L.4: He subdues peoples under us, and nations under our feet.

R.4: He let us win against other peoples and put nations under our control.

decisions.choice: He subdues: what God did for Israel
decisions.reason: The verb form can describe a past act, a habit or a wish. Read with verse 5, it recalls how God gave Israel the land, driving out the nations before them.

decisions.choice: peoples under us: brought under God's rule
decisions.reason: The nations that were subdued are the same nations called to clap for God in verse 2: in the end they gather as his people (verse 10).

decisions.choice: subdues: makes submit
decisions.reason: The verb (dabar, causative) is rare; it means to bring under control (18:48).

decisions.choice: let us win against
decisions.reason: Readable puts the verse in the past, the reading of m1.

records.source: יִבְחַר־לָ֥נוּ אֶת־נַחֲלָתֵ֑נוּ אֶ֥ת גְּא֨וֹן יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲשֶׁר־אָהֵ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: He chooses for us our inheritance, [the] pride of Jacob whom he loved. Selah.
pieces: He picked out our heritage for us, the glory of Jacob, the one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved. Selah

L.5: He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved. Selah

R.5: He chose a land for us to live in. It is the land Jacob's family was proud of. He loved Jacob's people. Selah

decisions.choice: our inheritance: the promised land
decisions.reason: The inheritance (nachalah) is the land God gave Israel to hold from generation to generation (Deuteronomy 4:21).

decisions.choice: the pride of Jacob: the land Jacob boasts of
decisions.reason: Here "pride" (ga'on) is the land Israel delights in. Elsewhere the phrase can mean Israel's arrogance (Amos 6:8), but not here.

decisions.choice: whom he loved: Jacob
decisions.reason: The one God loved is Jacob, the people descended from him (Malachi 1:2).

decisions.choice: a land for us to live in
decisions.reason: Readable says what the inheritance is (m1).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: עָלָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים בִּתְרוּעָ֑ה יְ֝הֹוָ֗ה בְּק֣וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃
records.gloss: God has gone up with a shout, YHWH with [the] sound of a ram's horn.
pieces: God has gone up amid shouting; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has gone up as the ram's horn sounds.

L.6: God has gone up with a shout, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with the sound of a ram's horn.

R.6: God has gone up to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne while the people shout. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} goes up while the trumpets blow.

decisions.choice: gone up: to his throne
alternatives: gone up to the temple with the ark
decisions.reason: The picture is of a king going up to take his throne (verse 9), as when the ark, the sign of God's presence, was carried up to Jerusalem "with shouting and the sound of the ram's horn" (2 Samuel 6:15).

decisions.choice: ram's horn: the shofar
decisions.reason: The shofar is a horn blown for signals and festivals, and at a king's coronation (1 Kings 1:39).

decisions.choice: a shout: the cheer for a king
decisions.reason: The word (teru'ah) is the cry of a crowd or the blast of horns, at battles and at coronations (Numbers 23:21).

decisions.choice: to his throne
decisions.reason: Readable says where God goes up (m1).

records.source: זַמְּר֣וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים זַמֵּ֑רוּ זַמְּר֖וּ לְמַלְכֵּ֣נוּ זַמֵּֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: Sing praises [to] God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises.
pieces: Make music to God, make music! Make music to our King, make music!

L.7: Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises.

R.7: Sing to God! Sing praises! Sing to our King! Sing praises!

decisions.choice: sing praises: make music in praise
decisions.reason: The verb (zamar) means to sing or play music in praise, often with instruments. Its four repetitions set the beat of the verse.

decisions.choice: our King: God
decisions.reason: The King is God, King of Israel and of all the earth (verse 8).

records.source: כִּ֤י מֶ֖לֶךְ כָּל־הָאָ֥רֶץ אֱלֹהִ֗ים זַמְּר֥וּ מַשְׂכִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: For King of all the earth [is] God; sing praises [with] a maskil.
pieces: For God reigns as King of all the earth; make music with a skillful psalm.

L.8: For God [is] King of all the earth; sing praises [with] a maskil.

R.8: God is the King of the whole world! Sing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a well-made song of praise.

decisions.choice: maskil: a skillful or teaching song
decisions.reason: The word (maskil) comes from a verb meaning to be wise or skillful. In titles it names a kind of psalm (32:1); here it may mean a well-crafted song, or singing with understanding. Its exact sense is unknown.

decisions.choice: a skillful psalm (B); a well-made song (R)
decisions.reason: In the body of a psalm Balanced and Readable give the likeliest sense (m1); Literal keeps the word.

records.source: מָלַ֣ךְ אֱ֭לֹהִים עַל־גּוֹיִ֑ם אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים יָשַׁ֤ב׀עַל־כִּסֵּ֬א קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: God reigns over nations; God sits on [the] throne of his holiness.
pieces: God now rules as King over the nations; upon {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy throne God sits.

L.9: God has become King over [the] nations; God sits on the throne of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness.

R.9: God has become King of all the nations. He sits on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy throne.

decisions.choice: reigns: has become King, has taken the throne
decisions.reason: The past form (malak) is the cry at a king's coronation, "He has become king" (2 Samuel 15:10; 1 Kings 1:11). God's going up (verse 6) is his enthronement over all the nations (compare 93:1; 97:1).

decisions.choice: his holy throne: his throne in heaven and in Zion
decisions.reason: God's throne is in heaven (11:4); the ark in the temple was its footstool on earth.

records.source: נְדִ֘יבֵ֤י עַמִּ֨ים׀נֶאֱסָ֗פוּ עַם֮ אֱלֹהֵ֪י אַבְרָ֫הָ֥ם כִּ֣י לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים מָֽגִנֵּי־אֶ֗רֶץ מְאֹ֣ד נַעֲלָֽה׃
records.gloss: Nobles of peoples have gathered, [the] people of [the] God of Abraham; for to God [belong the] shields of earth; exceedingly he is exalted.
pieces: The princes of the peoples come together to be the people of Abraham's God. For the shields of the earth are God's; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is raised high above all.

L.10: [The] nobles of [the] peoples have gathered, [the] people of the God of Abraham; for the shields of [the] earth [belong] to God; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is greatly exalted.

R.10: Leaders from many nations come together and join the people of Abraham's God. All the rulers of the world belong to God. He is honored far above everyone.

decisions.choice: the people of the God of Abraham: what the nobles become
alternatives: with the people of the God of Abraham
with the God of Abraham (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the two phrases side by side: the nobles of the nations gather as the people of Abraham's God. With a small change of one letter it would read "with the people", and the ancient Greek translation has "with the God of Abraham". The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: the God of Abraham: the promise to the nations
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham that all the families of the earth would be blessed through him (Genesis 12:3). The psalm sees the nations gathering to Abraham's God.

decisions.choice: the shields of the earth: its rulers
decisions.reason: Kings were called the shields of their people, who protected them (89:19; Hosea 4). The rulers of the earth belong to God.

decisions.choice: the rulers of the world
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m3).
